clue.text: Work colleague, receiving a flower, taken aback

indicators.note: the colleague takes the flower into the middle of himself, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a mate is a fellow worker or colleague

indicators.note: taken aback suggests something turned round to face backwards, so the flower phrase is read in reverse

parts.note: a lupin is a garden flower with tall spikes

explanation.surface: An office worker, handed a flower by a colleague, is startled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' reads as a noun beside 'colleague', but it is the verb definition; 'taken aback' reverses only the flower phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To work something, such as a puppet or a lever, is to handle and control it skilfully.

clue.text: Petulance displayed by love god in confusion

indicators.note: in places the love god pieces inside the word for confusion

parts.note: a mess is a state of confusion or disorder
love is nil in tennis scoring, shown as the letter O
Odin is the chief god of Norse mythology

explanation.surface: Cupid is sulking because everything around him is muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love god' looks like Cupid or Eros, but it splits into O (love, zero in tennis) and ODIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Petulance is sulky ill temper, which is what being prone to changeable moods shows.

clue.text: Annoyed, led off, making demand

indicators.note: off tells us the following word is taken away from the synonym for annoyed

parts.note: needled means irritated or annoyed

explanation.surface: Someone irritated after being led away starts making demands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes the letters LED from NEEDLED.
explanation.definitionFit: A need is a requirement, something called for, much as a demand is.

clue.text: Inducement taken up to break into building? That's sad

indicators.note: to break into means one piece forces its way inside another

parts.note: a pile is a large imposing building

indicators.note: in a down clue taken up means the word is read from bottom to top, so reversed

parts.note: bait is a lure or inducement

explanation.surface: Someone offered a bribe to burgle a house thinks it rather pathetic.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a pile is a building only in the sense of a grand house.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pitiable deserves pity, so it is sad or pathetic in the sense of being lamentable.

clue.text: Allowed to run away

definitions.meaning: slang for legitimate, so permitted or allowed
British slang for to run off or flee

explanation.definitionFit: The slang adjective means lawful or permitted, and the two-word verb phrase means to flee on foot.

clue.text: Work outside university room causing disturbance

indicators.note: outside means the word for work wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: toil means hard work

explanation.surface: Building work around a college room is causing a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Turmoil is a state of great confusion or agitation, a kind of upheaval.

clue.text: Corrupt officer imprisoned by a just judge

indicators.note: imprisoned by means the officer is shut inside the word for just

parts.note: due means deserved or just, as in getting one's due reward
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer
to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: A crooked policeman is locked up by a fair-minded judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corrupt officer' reads as one phrase, but 'Corrupt' is the verb definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To adulterate is to make impure by adding inferior material, i.e. to debase or spoil.

clue.text: Bodyguard in unsettled sector

indicators.note: unsettled signals that the letters of the next word are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A bodyguard is posted in a troubled part of town.
explanation.definitionFit: An escort is a person or group accompanying someone for protection.

clue.text: Beauty seen by a saint as false

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person
a means one, a single

explanation.surface: A beautiful woman spotted with a holy person is judged to be a fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishonest means untruthful or deceitful, so false in the sense of not genuine.

clue.text: Country without any seed

indicators.note: without tells us to take the next word out of the country name

parts.note: Germany is a European country

explanation.surface: A nation with no grain to plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A germ is the embryo or origin from which something grows, as in wheat germ.

clue.text: Chance to participate in card game with family

parts.note: loo is an old card game, played for stakes
kin means one's family or relatives

explanation.surface: Joining a family card game gives you a chance to play.
explanation.walkthrough: LOO is also British slang for a toilet; here it is the card game.
explanation.definitionFit: A look-in is an informal word for an opportunity to take part or succeed.

clue.text: Tending to find fault, I act up so fretfully

indicators.note: fretfully suggests agitation, telling us to jumble the preceding letters

explanation.surface: A grumbler confesses to behaving badly when anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: Captious describes someone fond of raising petty objections, a nit-picker.

clue.text: Certainly upset, admitting delay, editor is idealistic

indicators.note: admitting means letting the delay into the middle of the other word
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word is reversed

parts.note: yes is an affirmative reply, certainly
to tarry is to linger or delay

explanation.surface: An upset editor, forced to accept a deadline extension, remains a dreamer.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' turns its word upside down, so it reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Starry-eyed means naively romantic or unrealistically optimistic, much like an idealist.

clue.text: Count faces end of influence after revolution

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word influence
after revolution means the word for faces is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: meets means confronts or faces

explanation.surface: An aristocrat confronts the loss of power after an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' looks like a nobleman; it is the verb, as in counting someone a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: To esteem someone highly is to count or reckon them worthy; both verbs mean to regard.

clue.text: Group of ships following group not well advanced

parts.note: f is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
a lot is a set or group of items
ill means unwell
A stands for advanced, as in A level

explanation.surface: A naval squadron trails another, its crews sick and pushing on.
explanation.definitionFit: A flotilla is a small fleet, a group of boats or ships sailing together.

clue.text: Bore, informed about period of history, starts to talk excessively

indicators.note: about means the word for informed goes around the other pieces

parts.note: told means informed someone
an era is a period of history

indicators.note: starts to picks the opening letters of the two following words

explanation.surface: A bore lectures endlessly on a historical age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' looks like a noun for a dull person; it is the past tense of bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Bore here is the past tense of bear, to put up with, which is what tolerated means.

clue.text: Rent once repaired in fabric

indicators.note: repaired suggests the torn letters are put back together in a new order

explanation.surface: A tear in a piece of cloth has been mended.
explanation.definitionFit: Cretonne is a heavy printed cotton cloth used for curtains and upholstery.

clue.text: Masters aim to let in new blood

indicators.note: to let in means the other pieces admit the new letter inside them

parts.note: aces are experts or masters at something
a try is an attempt or aim

explanation.surface: Old masters try to bring fresh blood into the team.
explanation.walkthrough: The new letter goes in after the first A of the joined pieces; 'blood' means lineage, not the fluid.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood means lineage or descent, as in being of royal blood, so it stands for one's line of forebears.

clue.text: Gear box?

definitions.meaning: British slang for clothes or equipment, one's kit
to box is to punch, and the slang word means to hit hard

explanation.definitionFit: The noun is British slang for belongings or clothing, and the verb means to beat or strike someone.

clue.text: Bird settled eastward of place

indicators.note: in an across clue eastward of means placed to the right, so after

parts.note: Pl is the abbreviation for place in street names
over means finished or settled, as when a matter is over

explanation.surface: A bird has come to rest to the east of a town.
explanation.definitionFit: The plover is a wading bird found on shores and open ground.

clue.text: Forgivable answer in row, volume rising

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters are read from the bottom up, reversed
in places the answer letter inside the word for row

parts.note: a line is a row of things

explanation.surface: A forgivable reply in an argument where the noise keeps rising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts A inside LINE to make LAINE; add V and 'rising' turns the lot round. 'row' looks like a quarrel; it is a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A venial sin is a minor one that can be pardoned, as opposed to a mortal sin.

clue.text: Evil feud about gold

indicators.note: about means the word for feud surrounds the word for gold

parts.note: enmity is hostility, the state of a feud
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A wicked quarrel breaks out over treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: ENORMITY strictly means wickedness, not great size, which makes 'Evil' a fair definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Enormity in its strict sense means great wickedness or an outrageous act.

clue.text: Reported grey matter obtained from the earth

indicators.note: reported means as spoken, so the word is one that sounds like another

parts.note: grey matter is informal for the brain or mind

explanation.surface: Brains are said to have been dug out of the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Coal or ore that is dug out by excavation has been extracted from underground.

clue.text: Unconventional fellow round middle of pageant

parts.note: a ring is a round shape

indicators.note: middle of picks the central letter of the seven-letter word pageant

explanation.surface: An oddball man circles the centre of a carnival.
explanation.definitionFit: Fringe as an adjective means outside the mainstream, as in fringe theatre.

clue.text: Giant effort to get up and about

indicators.note: in a down clue to get up means the word rises, reading backwards

parts.note: a go is an attempt or effort
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A giant makes an effort to stand up and walk around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get up' turns GO into OG.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a monstrous man-eating giant of folk tales.

clue.text: Sailor in drama back in port

indicators.note: back means the letters built so far are read in reverse
in puts the sailor inside the word for drama

parts.note: No (also Noh) is classical Japanese drama
AB, able seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor in a play returns to harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' gives NABO, and 'back' turns it round. OBAN is a ferry port on the west coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Oban is a harbour town in Argyll, serving the Hebridean islands.

clue.text: Bargain, almost fresh, obtained by one and consumed

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: new means fresh
got means obtained
I is the Roman numeral for one
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: A fresh bargain picked up by someone and eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: To bargain is to haggle over terms, to try to reach an agreement by discussion.

clue.text: Big deer had reassembled in strong position

indicators.note: reassembled says the letters of the words before it are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A large stag has been put back together in a sturdy pose.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridgehead is a fortified foothold established in enemy territory, a secure military position.
